claims.operation: Successful plain SET replacement, no expiry option
claims.version: Redis 7.2.0 confirmed; option history in live SET reference
claims.default_configuration: Default plain SET does not retain TTL
claims.type_domain: SET creates a string and overwrites prior hash or string; successful SET with GET has a separate old-type constraint
claims.exceptions: An unmet NX/XX condition is not a successful replacement and returns before modifying the key. Explicit EX/PX and EXAT/PXAT set a deadline in their respective units; KEEPTTL retains an existing one.

claims.type_domain: Replaces value with a string; expiry options are mutually exclusive. Absent/persistent keys have no retained deadline.
claims.exceptions: Retains absolute expiry, rather than refreshing the timeout. Conditional SET must actually succeed; after logical expiry, an ordinary lookup can remove the old key first.

claims.subject: Persistent session key, either string or hash
claims.version: GT/NX/XX/LT since 7.0.0, available in 7.2; tagged source inspected
claims.default_configuration: Persistent is treated as infinite for GT; no finite extension can exceed it
claims.type_domain: Type-independent key expiry; integer seconds; representable expiry required. EXPIRE accepts non-positive durations too, but that is not the finite-positive premise here.
claims.exceptions: Missing key returns 0; GT on an already volatile key compares requested absolute deadline with current deadline and rejects earlier/equal values. NX requires an existing key lacking expiry.
claims.corrected_wording_assessment: Persistent-key rejection and NX alternative are correct; saying GT tightens a finite expiry reverses its direction (F1).
claims.validation: Proposed GT-on-persistent=0 and NX=1 assertions are sound, but do not exercise the erroneous finite-TTL direction.

claims.operation: Successful unconditional EXPIRE key 0 versus ordinary deadline expiration
claims.version: Redis 7.2.0 event-generating branches and configuration checked
claims.default_configuration: Notifications disabled by default; E plus generic/expired classes needed to observe both keyevent streams; KEA includes the necessary 7.2 classes
claims.type_domain: EXPIRE is type-independent; seconds=0 causes immediate deletion on the primary under normal command execution

material_findings.title: Claim 4 corrected wording reverses the action of EXPIRE GT
material_findings.candidate_text: GT only tightens keys that already have a finite TTL.
material_findings.judgment: The refusal to attach a finite expiry to a persistent key is correct, but tightening an existing timeout means shortening its deadline; GT only accepts a strictly later deadline and therefore extends it. LT is the shortening condition. The candidate includes the correct greater-than definition earlier, leaving its required final correction internally inconsistent.
material_findings.consequence: Documentation using this correction can choose GT to shorten a session lifetime and get 0 instead; an extension can succeed when the author expects a tightening-only rule.
material_findings.checked_bounded_wording: On an existing persistent key EXPIRE key seconds GT returns 0. On an existing volatile key it changes the deadline only if the requested absolute deadline is strictly later; it extends rather than shortens that deadline. NX can set expiry on an existing persistent key; a missing key still returns 0.
material_findings.materiality_basis: The assignment expressly requires corrected bounded wording and exact operation applicability for every claim. This is a direction error in that correction, rather than a locator defect.
material_findings.validation_status: Independent documentation and tagged source inspection; no Redis service execution.

material_findings.title: The KEEPTTL acceptance check requires an unsupported strict drop in integer TTL
material_findings.candidate_section: Acceptance checks for the service, check 1
material_findings.candidate_text: TTL sess:42 > 0 (smaller than before the KEEPTTL write)
material_findings.judgment: KEEPTTL preserves the deadline, while TTL reports rounded integer seconds in Redis 7.2.0. A correct fast write can leave the two reported values equal; elapsed time need not cross a seconds rounding boundary. The listed sequence also supplies no explicit before measurement. Positivity alone does not show the original deadline was retained rather than reset.

counterexample.method: Static arithmetic from the independently inspected tagged implementation: (remaining_ms+500)//1000; not a deployed-service measurement.

material_findings.consequence: Using the smaller-than condition as the acceptance oracle can fail a compliant service. Using only positivity can pass a service that incorrectly replaces the original expiration.
material_findings.checked_bounded_validation: A prospective deadline-preservation check can compare PEXPIRETIME before and after the successful KEEPTTL write while also checking the new value, isolating the key from competing writers and using an expiry safely in the future. Redis 7.2.0 implements PEXPIRETIME through the absolute-millisecond branch. This is an assessment of an appropriate oracle, not a repair or executed check.
material_findings.materiality_basis: Two concrete service acceptance checks are required; this check supplies a false rejection condition for its central KEEPTTL behavior.
material_findings.validation_status: Tagged-source reasoning and a static arithmetic counterexample only; service check proposed, not executed.
